drhp.business: PBM Polytex Limited manufactures cotton yarn at two spinning units, one at Petlad, Gujarat and a second at Borgaon, District Chhindwara, Madhya Pradesh. The Company also generates renewable power for captive use through windmills and rooftop solar plants, and exports a portion of its cotton yarn output.
drhp.expansion: The Company commenced an Open-End Modernization Project at its spinning operations: civil and building works were completed, and supporting utilities (power connection, humidification systems, compressed-air infrastructure) were made fully operational. The Auto Leveler Draw Frame and the new Open-End machine were received and commissioned in the early part of the following financial year, with the project fully completed by mid-July 2026, expected to deliver an improved realization of approximately ₹5-6 per kg over existing production. Subject to successful market acceptance, a proposal to install a second Open-End machine together with an additional Draw Frame is under consideration for September-December 2026. Separately, on the renewable-energy side, the Phase II Solar Plant at the Petlad Unit was commissioned in May 2025, adding to the earlier Phase I Solar Plant; a further solar installation of approximately 250 KVA at the Petlad Unit is under evaluation, subject to space availability.

litigation.note: Long-pending labour dispute at the BLP Unit was resolved via an out-of-court settlement during the year, duly filed and accepted by the Hon'ble High Court (per MD&A/Directors' Report).

The Auto Leveler Draw Frame and the new Open-End machine were received and commissioned in the early part of the following financial year, with the project fully completed by mid-July 2026, expected to deliver an improved realization of approximately ₹5-6 per kg over existing production. moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body: cost position: Captive solar power generation structurally reduces energy costs — evidence: Phase II Solar Plant commissioned May 2025 at a cost of ₹54 Lakhs, expected to generate about 9.95 lakh units per annum with projected savings of about ₹10 Lakhs per year, adding to Phase I Solar Plant savings of about ₹66 Lakhs per year.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Cotton remains a rain-dependent crop, vulnerable to climatic and policy shifts, exposing raw-material availability and cost to weather variability.
- Rising Minimum Support Price and import duties continue to inflate input costs, following a 7.6% MSP hike that kept domestic cotton prices elevated above international benchmarks.
- U.S. tariffs on Indian textile exports escalated to 50% effective 27 August 2025, threatening export demand and sharply reducing export viability, particularly for cotton yarn.
- Both units face a shortage of skilled workers and high absenteeism (industry-wide 11-20% daily), constraining capacity utilisation; the Petlad Unit ran at approximately 52-55% utilisation for much of the year due to this constraint.
- The 11% import duty on raw cotton continued to distort competitiveness, with only a temporary waiver during August-December 2025 offering short-term relief, indicating the underlying cost disadvantage could return.
- International cotton prices remained subdued while domestic prices stayed elevated, creating a significant and sustained cost gap for domestic spinners that compresses yarn margins.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continued renewable-energy (solar) investment to structurally reduce power costs.
- Policy advocacy for permanent removal of the cotton import duty to align domestic input costs with global benchmarks.
- Diversification of export markets to mitigate concentration and tariff risk.
- Modernisation of the Open-End line to improve product quality and per-kg realisation.
